extracted.intended_audience: NCPC staff, Federal and District agencies, applicants, and members of the public participating in NCPC NEPA and FOIA processes
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedural criteria the National Capital Planning Commission (NCPC) uses to determine NEPA applicability (Categorical Exclusions, EAs, EISs), the contents and public process for EAs/EISs/RODs, supplemental document triggers, and NCPC FOIA policies and definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extraordinary Circumstances precluding a Categorical Exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: A categorical exclusion shall not be applied if there is a reasonable likelihood of any extraordinary circumstance listed (examples shown include potential to violate law/E.O.; significant increase in surface transportation congestion; degrading air quality; impacting water quality or public water supply; disproportionately high adverse effect on low income/minority populations; degrading unsatisfactory environmental conditions; establishing a precedent with potentially significant effects; or other unique circumstances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Executive Director must include in the EDR (or documentation of a delegated action) the decision to apply a Categorical Exclusion including consideration of possible Extraordinary Circumstances or to not apply one because of Extraordinary Circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorical Exclusion — installation/restoration of onsite electrical distribution systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of the installation or restoration of onsite primary or secondary electrical distribution systems including minor solar panel arrays may be categorically excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as §601.12(a)(1); actions not listed are not eligible even if they meet general criteria in §601.10(b). Executive Director must document rationale in EDR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorical Exclusion — minor site elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of installation or restoration of minor site elements (e.g., identification signs, sidewalks, patios, fences, curbs, retaining walls, landscaping, trail or stream improvements), and water/sewer lines that are replacement in kind may be categorically excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as §601.12(a)(2); includes additional features and replacement-in-kind work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorical Exclusion — minor building elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of the installation or restoration of minor building elements (e.g., windows, doors, roofs, building signs, rooftop equipment, green roofs) may be categorically excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as §601.12(a)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorical Exclusion — adoption/amendment of Federal Element or policy/feasibility plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Adoption of a Federal Element of the Comprehensive Plan or amendments thereto or broad-based policy or feasibility plans prepared and adopted by the Commission in response to the Comprehensive Plan may be categorically excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as §601.12(a)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorical Exclusion — installation of communication antennae consistent with GSA bulletin
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of installation of communication antennae on Federal buildings and co-location of commercial antennas on Federal property consistent with GSA Bulletin FMR D–242 may be categorically excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as §601.12(a)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorical Exclusion — new construction/building expansion with limited impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of proposals for new construction, building expansion, or improvements to existing facilities may be categorically excluded when: (i) in compliance with local/state/Federal requirements; (ii) site and scale consistent with adjacent buildings; (iii) proposed use will not substantially increase motor vehicles in vicinity; and (iv) little/no unresolved resource conflicts or community controversy related to environmental concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as §601.12(a)(6); all four conditions must apply for this categorical exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorical Exclusion — transfers of jurisdiction without land-use change
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of transfers of jurisdiction pursuant to 40 U.S.C. 8124 that are not anticipated to result in changes in land-use and that have no potential for environmental impact may be categorically excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as §601.12(a)(7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorical Exclusion — minor modification to a General Development Plan (Capper-Cramton lands)
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of a minor modification to a General Development Plan applicable to lands acquired pursuant to the Capper-Cramton Act when non-significant environmental impacts are anticipated may be categorically excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as §601.12(a)(8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorical Exclusion — reorganization of NCPC
rubrics_metrics.description: Reorganization of the NCPC may be categorically excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as §601.12(a)(9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorical Exclusion — personnel actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel actions (e.g., investigations; performance reviews; awards; personal service contracts; promotions; reductions in force; reassignments; relocations; employee supervision and training) may be categorically excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorical Exclusion — legal activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal activities (e.g., legal advice and opinions; litigation or dispute resolution; procurement of outside legal services) may be categorically excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorical Exclusion — routine administration/operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities related to routine and continuing administration, management, maintenance and operations of the Commission or its facilities may be categorically excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicitly listed as part of §601.12 (text preceding item 13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorical Exclusion — issuance of rules, policies, guides, publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Adoption and issuance of rules, directives, official policies, guidelines, publications or recommendations of an educational, financial, informational, legal, technical or procedural nature may be categorically excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation requirement for Categorical Exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Director must include in the EDR, or the documentation of a delegated action, the decision to apply a Categorical Exclusion and the rationale for that decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in §601.12(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: EA purpose and core contents
rubrics_metrics.description: An Environmental Assessment (EA) is a concise document that includes a brief discussion of the proposed action; the purpose and need; environmental impacts of the proposed action; environmental impacts of alternatives considered; mitigation measures, if necessary; and a list of agencies and persons consulted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must provide sufficient information and analysis to enable the Executive Director to determine whether to issue a FONSI or prepare an EIS (§601.15(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of actions eligible for an EA
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions that generally require an EA exhibit: (1) minor but likely insignificant degradation of environmental quality; (2) minor but likely insignificant cumulative impact on environmental quality; and (3) minor but likely insignificant impact on protected resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the typical characteristics described in §601.13(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public involvement in EA preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall involve applicants; Federal and District agencies; the public; and stakeholders to the extent practicable in preparing an EA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public scoping may be undertaken at the sole discretion of the Executive Director; if used, NCPC must issue public notice (media with widespread circulation and NCPC website) stating intent to prepare an EA and include date/time/location of public scoping meeting (§601.15(b)–(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft EA public comment period
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC may solicit public review and comment of a Draft EA; the public comment period generally shall be thirty (30) calendar days, beginning when the Executive Director announces availability of the Draft EA on NCPC's website. NCPC may decline to circulate a Draft EA for non-controversial projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in §601.15(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: FONSI content and timing when NCPC is Lead Agency
rubrics_metrics.description: If the final EA supports a FONSI, NCPC shall prepare and execute a FONSI that briefly states reasons why the proposed action will not have a significant effect and includes the EA or summary, any mitigation commitments, and a schedule for implementing mitigation commitments; the FONSI shall be signed following Commission final approval of the applicant's project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare FONSI after close of discretionary public comment on Draft EA or at conclusion of EA if no comment period (§601.16(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: NCPC evaluation of Lead Agency FONSI when NCPC is not Lead
rubrics_metrics.description: If NCPC is not the Lead Agency, NCPC shall evaluate the adequacy of the Lead Agency's FONSI; if adequate, NCPC may co-sign the Lead Agency's FONSI following Commission final approval or prepare and execute its own FONSI consistent with paragraph (a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure described in §601.16(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of certain FONSIs and publication timing
rubrics_metrics.description: In certain limited circumstances, a FONSI prepared by NCPC shall be available for public review for thirty (30) days before final determination; NCPC shall publish all FONSIs on its website seven (7) calendar days before the Commission takes action on the underlying application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §601.16(c) for applicability and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: EA supplemental triggers and process
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall prepare a supplemental EA if five or more years have elapsed since adoption of the EA and there are substantial changes to the proposed action relevant to environmental concerns or significant new circumstances or information relevant to environmental concerns; NCPC may supplement an EA at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When supplementing, NCPC shall prepare, circulate, and file a supplement and adopt a FONSI in accordance with §§601.15 and 601.16; if not Lead Agency, proceed as in §601.16(b)–(c) (§601.17).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for an EIS prior to approval of major Federal actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to the Commission's approval of a major Federal action significantly affecting the quality of the human environment, the Executive Director shall prepare an EIS for a Non-Federal Agency application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General requirement stated in §601.18.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance determination — context and intensity
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall determine whether an EIS is required and whether impacts are significant by considering the context (effects on society as a whole, National Capital Region, particular interests, specific locality) and intensity (severity) of impacts, informed by 40 CFR 1508.27(a)–(b) and Commission plans and programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals conflicting with Commission plans/programs are more likely to be significant; severity evaluated per 40 CFR 1508.27(b)(1)–(10) (§601.19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific characteristics that make an action significant
rubrics_metrics.description: An action shall be deemed significant and require an EIS if it: (1) results in a substantial change to the Monumental Core; (2) causes substantial alteration to important historical, cultural, and natural features of the National Capital and its Environs; or (3) is likely to be controversial because of its impacts on the human environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated in §601.19(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: EIS streamlining techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC as Lead Agency shall use techniques to minimize EIS length, including drafting in clear, concise language; preparing an analytic versus encyclopedic EIS; reducing emphasis on background information; using scoping to emphasize significant issues; incorporating information by reference; using programmatic EIS and tiering to eliminate duplication; and following format guidelines (§601.22).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to focus the EIS on significant, decision-relevant information (§601.20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic Environmental Documents and tiering
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a programmatic Environmental Document (PEA/PEIS) to assess impacts when there is uncertainty regarding timing, location and environmental impacts of subsequent implementing actions; when undertaking site- or project-specific actions within parameters of a PEA/PEIS, NCPC shall tier its Environmental Document by summarizing information in the PEIS/PEA and concentrating on issues applicable to the specific action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PEAs/PEISs prepared by NCPC are governed by CEQ regulations and these rules (§601.21).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of an EIS — cover sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: The EIS cover sheet shall be one page and include list of responsible and Cooperating Agencies; title of proposed action; NCPC point of contact (name, address, telephone); designation as draft/final/supplement; a one-paragraph abstract; and the date by which comments must be received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as §601.22(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of an EIS — summary
rubrics_metrics.description: The summary shall accurately summarize the information presented in the EIS, focusing on main conclusions, areas of controversy, and issues to be resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as §601.22(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of an EIS — table of contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The table of contents shall allow readers to quickly locate subject matter in the EIS by topic area and/or alternatives analyzed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as §601.22(a)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of an EIS — purpose and need statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The EIS shall include a brief statement of the purpose of and need for the action, stating the underlying purpose and need to which the agency responds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as §601.22(a)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of an EIS — identification of alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: The EIS shall identify alternatives including the proposed action and the no-action alternative; provide description and supporting documentation for all alternatives (including those not within agency jurisdiction); identify alternatives considered but eliminated and reasons; state the agency's preferred alternative, if any; identify the environmentally preferred alternative; and list mitigation measures not already in the proposed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive treatment of alternatives is required (§601.22(a)(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of an EIS — affected environment
rubrics_metrics.description: The EIS shall provide a succinct description of the environment to be affected by the proposed action and alternatives, including other activities in the area affected by or related to the proposed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as §601.22(a)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of an EIS — environmental consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The EIS shall focus on environmental impacts of alternatives including: adverse effects that cannot be avoided; relationship between short-term uses and maintenance/enhancement of long-term productivity; irreversible commitments of resources; discussion of direct, indirect and cumulative effects and their significance; and appropriate mitigation measures. It shall also disclose issues/impact topics considered but dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resource areas/issues to consider include (without limitation): conflicts with land use plans; natural/biological resources (topography, hydrology, soils, flora/fauna, floodplains, wetlands, endangered species); air quality; noise; water resources (wastewater, stormwater); utilities and energy; solid/hazardous waste; community facilities; housing; transportation network; socio-cultural and economic environments; Environmental Justice (EO 12898); urban quality/design/visual resources; historic/cultural resources (including Section 106 results); public health and safety (§601.22(a)(7) and subitems i–xv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of an EIS — list of preparers
rubrics_metrics.description: The EIS shall include a list of all pertinent organizations, agencies, individuals, and government representatives primarily responsible for EIS preparation and their qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as §601.22(a)(8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of an EIS — index
rubrics_metrics.description: The EIS shall include an index structured to reasonably assist readers in identifying and locating major topic areas or elements of EIS information, with sufficient detail to focus on areas of interest to any reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as §601.22(a)(9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of an EIS — appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendices shall consist of material prepared in connection with an EIS (distinct from material incorporated by reference) that substantiate any analysis fundamental to the EIS; appendices shall be analytical and relevant to the decision and shall be posted on NCPC's website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation in EIS preparation and scoping procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall involve the applicant, Federal and District agencies, the public and stakeholders in EIS preparation; public participation is required for Public Scoping and review of the Draft EIS. To determine scope through Public Scoping NCPC shall: disseminate a NOI in accordance with 40 CFR 1501.7 and 1506.6; publish a NOI in the FEDERAL REGISTER and on NCPC's website; include date/time/location of scoping meeting; announce meeting at least 30 calendar days in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoping meetings must be in accessible facilities, include translators/signers if requested in advance, and allow special arrangements for consultation with affected Indian tribes or Native American groups; consider all comments received during announced comment period regarding alternatives, affected environment, and potential impacts; apply provisions to Supplemental EIS where Executive Director determines scoping required (§601.23(b)(1)–(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft EIS public comment period and meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: A Draft EIS shall be available for public review and comment for generally forty-five (45) calendar days, beginning when NCPC shares a copy with EPA in anticipation of EPA's NOA; NCPC shall hold at least one public meeting during the comment period, announced at least 30 calendar days in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in §601.23(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final EIS response to comments and Commission review period
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final EIS shall respond to oral and written comments received during the Draft EIS public comment period. The Commission shall take final action following a thirty (30) day Commission-sponsored review period of the Final EIS, starting when EPA publishes a NOA for the Final EIS in the FEDERAL REGISTER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in §601.24(a)–(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of Decision content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A ROD prepared when NCPC is Lead and recommending approval must state the decision; identify alternatives considered and those environmentally preferable; discuss preferences among alternatives based on relevant factors (including economic/technical planning and Commission mission) and factors balanced; state whether all practicable means to avoid/minimize environmental harm have been adopted (and if not, why); include a monitoring and enforcement program summarizing mitigation measures; date of issuance; and Chairman's signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Draft ROD contents must be summarized in the EDR and a full draft included as an Appendix; the Draft ROD shall be made available to the public for review 14 calendar days prior to Commission consideration; the Commission decision shall be made in a public meeting of record (§601.25(a)(1)–(2),(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when NCPC is not Lead for ROD
rubrics_metrics.description: If NCPC is not the Lead Agency, following Commission final approval NCPC may co-sign the Lead Agency's ROD if it agrees with contents and conclusions, or prepare, sign and adopt its own ROD in accordance with the ROD requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in §601.25(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental EIS triggers and process
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall prepare a supplemental EIS if five or more years have elapsed since adoption of the EIS and there are substantial changes to the proposed action relevant to environmental concerns or significant new circumstances or information relevant to environmental concerns; NCPC may supplement an EIS at any time to further NEPA purposes; public scoping is optional for a supplemental EIS; NCPC shall prepare a ROD for a Supplemental EIS consistent with §601.25.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in §601.26(a)–(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative EIS for NCPC-initiated draft legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Director shall prepare an EIS for draft legislation initiated by NCPC for submission to Congress, consistent with 40 CFR 1506.8; the EIS shall be included as part of formal transmittal of NCPC's legislative proposal to Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement stated in §601.27(a); not required for legislation Congress directs NCPC to prepare (§601.27(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: NCPC FOIA policy to maximize information availability
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC's policy is to facilitate the broadest possible availability and dissemination of information to the public through its website and physical distribution of materials; NCPC staff should assist the public in obtaining information formally or informally not inconsistent with the rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCPC shall, to the maximum extent possible, make available agency records of interest to the public appropriate for disclosure (§602.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Adverse Determination under FOIA
rubrics_metrics.description: An Adverse Determination includes a determination to withhold, in whole or in part, records requested; failure to respond to all aspects of a request; denial of fee waiver; denial of expedited processing; or challenges to adequacy of description, absence of responsive records, or adequacy of search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition provided for FOIA processing and appeals (§602.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Agency Record
rubrics_metrics.description: An Agency Record means any documentary material created or obtained by a federal agency in transaction of agency business and under agency control (e.g., books, papers, maps, plats, plans, drawings, photographs, machine-readable materials, electronic records including email, audio-visual material); generally excludes records created/maintained primarily for staff convenience and withheld from other agency employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provided to clarify what materials are subject to FOIA (§602.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Confidential Commercial Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential Commercial Information means commercial or financial information obtained by NCPC from a submitter that may be protected under FOIA Exemption 4 (trade secrets and commercial/financial information obtained from a person that is privileged or confidential).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate withholding under Exemption 4 (§602.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Controlled Unclassified Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Controlled Unclassified Information is unclassified information not meeting national security classification standards but pertinent to national interests or important interests of entities outside the federal government and requiring protection/special handling under law or policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies handling requirements for non-classified but sensitive records (§602.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Commercial Use Request
rubrics_metrics.description: A Commercial Use Request is a FOIA request from or on behalf of someone seeking information to further commercial, trade, or profit interests of the requester or the person on whose behalf the request is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine fee category and processing priorities (§602.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Direct Costs for FOIA processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct Costs are expenditures NCPC incurs in searching for, duplicating, and reviewing documents to respond to a FOIA request (e.g., salary of employee performing work (basic rate + 16% benefits) and cost of operating duplicating machinery); excludes overhead like space, heating, lighting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to calculate fees (§602.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Duplication means making a copy of a document necessary to respond to a FOIA request in a form reasonably usable by the requester (paper, audio-visual materials, machine-readable documents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant for fee calculation and production format (§602.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Educational Institution requester category
rubrics_metrics.description: Educational Institution includes preschools, K–12, institutions of undergraduate/graduate/professional/vocational education that operate a program of scholarly research; to qualify, requester must show request is made under auspices of qualifying institution and records are not sought for commercial use but to further scholarly research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine fee category (§602.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Expedited Processing for FOIA
rubrics_metrics.description: Expedited Processing means giving a FOIA request priority because the requester has shown a compelling need for the records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards and procedures for granting expedited processing are defined in the FOIA part (§602.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Fee Waiver under FOIA
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee Waiver is a waiver in whole or in part of fees if requester demonstrates statutory requirements including that the information is in the public interest and not requested primarily for commercial purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate fee waiver requests (§602.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — FOIA Public Liaison
rubrics_metrics.description: FOIA Public Liaison is an NCPC official responsible for assisting in reducing delays, increasing transparency and understanding the status of requests, and assisting in resolution of disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Role defined to aid requesters and improve FOIA administration (§602.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — FOIA Request form/means
rubrics_metrics.description: FOIA Request means a written request by an entity or member of the public for an Agency Record submitted via USPS mail or other delivery means including electronic-mail or facsimile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies acceptable submission formats for FOIA requests (§602.3).
